name: Gongura Pachadi
description: A tangy, spicy relish of sorrel (gongura) leaves lightly cooked and ground with red chillies, garlic and spices, often pickled for keeping. It is considered a quintessential part of Andhra cuisine, and Guntur gongura is especially prized.
how_to_eat: Mix a little into hot rice with ghee.
how_to_order: Ask for gongura pachadi with an Andhra meals plate, or buy it in jars at pickle shops.

name: Avakaya
description: A sharp raw-mango pickle with mustard powder, red chilli powder and sesame oil, made once a year in summer. Mudda pappu (plain dal) with avakaya is a classic first bite of an Andhra meal.
how_to_eat: Mix a small piece with rice, dal and ghee.
how_to_order: It comes with Andhra meals; jars are sold at pickle and sweet shops.

name: Pesarattu
description: A crepe of soaked and ground green gram with green chilli and ginger, made without urad dal and not fermented. Originating in coastal Andhra, it is a breakfast staple; the version stuffed with upma (upma pesarattu) is especially popular.
how_to_eat: Eat it hot with ginger chutney.
how_to_order: Ask for 'pesarattu' or 'upma pesarattu' at a tiffin centre in the morning.

name: Pulihora
description: Tamarind rice tempered with mustard seeds, peanuts, curry leaves and green chillies. It is served at festivals and family events and is a common temple prasadam.
how_to_eat: Eat it at room temperature, by hand.
how_to_order: Ask for pulihora as prasadam at temples or with festival meals.

name: Punugulu
description: Deep-fried balls of rice and urad dal batter, often made from leftover idli or dosa batter, with onion and green chillies. A common street snack across delta Andhra.
how_to_eat: Eat them hot with coconut or peanut chutney.
how_to_order: Ask for a plate of 'punugulu' at an evening snack cart or tiffin centre.

name: Bongu Chicken
description: A tribal dish of chicken marinated with salt, chilli, turmeric and ginger-garlic and cooked inside bamboo over charcoal, with no oil or water. It is strongly associated with Araku Valley and Maredumilli.
how_to_eat: Eat it hot, straight from the split bamboo.
how_to_order: Ask for 'bongu chicken' or 'bamboo chicken' at roadside stalls around Araku Valley.

name: Tirupati Laddu
description: The prasadam laddu of the Venkateswara temple at Tirumala, made of gram flour, ghee, sugar, sugar candy, cashews, raisins and cardamom. Also called Srivari laddu, it received a GI tag in 2009.
how_to_eat: Eat it as prasadam; break off a piece and share it.
how_to_order: Collect it at the temple laddu counters with a darshan token; without one, show Aadhaar to buy up to two a day.

name: Pootharekulu
description: Paper-thin sheets of rice starch layered with powdered sugar or jaggery and ghee, sometimes with dry fruits. The name means 'coated sheets'. It is from Atreyapuram village in the Godavari region and received a GI tag in 2023-24.
how_to_eat: Eat gently by hand; the sheets crumble easily.
how_to_order: Ask for 'Atreyapuram pootharekulu' at sweet shops, sold boxed by the piece.

name: Bandar Laddu
description: A laddu of Bengal gram flour, jaggery syrup and ghee from Machilipatnam (Bandar), also called thokkudu laddu. It was registered as a GI foodstuff in 2017.
how_to_eat: Eat it as is; it is soft and crumbly.
how_to_order: Ask for 'Bandar laddu' or 'thokkudu laddu' at Machilipatnam sweet shops.

name: Kakinada Kaja
description: A layered fried pastry of wheat flour soaked in sugar syrup, dry on the outside and juicy inside. It is from the coastal town of Kakinada.
how_to_eat: Bite carefully; the syrup bursts out.
how_to_order: Ask for 'Kakinada kaja' by the piece or weight at sweet shops.
